title: Build Your Own LLM
outcomeTitle: Build a tiny language model that writes
outcome: A tiny language model you build and train yourself in Python, right in your browser.
description: ChatGPT can feel like magic. It isn't: it turns text into numbers, predicts the next piece, and picks one. You'll build each step yourself in Python, from your own tokenizer to a model you train on text you choose, and see why its answers vary and how attention lets it read context.
studyNote: No setup: the Python runs in your browser. Some coding helps, but Pedro explains every step.

highlights.label: Tokens
highlights.desc: How text becomes numbers, and why GPT splits words into pieces

highlights.label: Next-token prediction
highlights.desc: A model that writes, built from counting

highlights.label: Temperature and attention
highlights.desc: Why answers vary, and how a model decides which words matter

highlights.label: Training
highlights.desc: Watch your own model's loss fall, then make it write

title: Build a Rocket to Space
outcomeTitle: Design a rocket that reaches space
outcome: A rocket you design and fly in a physics simulator that carries a payload past the 100 km edge of space.
description: Why does a rocket work in empty space? Why do real rockets drop pieces on the way up? You'll design rockets, predict how high they'll go, launch them in a physics simulator, and work out where the fuel's energy went, until your own design carries a payload into space.
studyNote: Predict first, then launch: the gap between the two is where you learn.

highlights.label: The rocket equation
highlights.desc: Why doubling the fuel doesn't double your speed

highlights.label: Gravity and air
highlights.desc: Where the speed goes on the way up

highlights.label: Mission
highlights.desc: Staging, then the lightest rocket you can get to 100 km

title: Build a Neuron, Then a Tiny Brain
outcomeTitle: Build a neuron that fires and a synapse that learns
outcome: A simulated neuron you drive and measure, a circuit that detects coincidences, and a synapse that learns.
description: Every thought runs on neurons that add up tiny electrical inputs and fire when they reach a threshold. You'll drive a simulated neuron, measure how it codes a stronger input, wire two inputs into a coincidence detector, and teach a synapse to link a bell to food, as in Pavlov's dogs.
studyNote: Each step is a small experiment: predict, run it, explain the result.

highlights.label: The neuron
highlights.desc: Resting potential, threshold and the leak

highlights.label: Spikes
highlights.desc: All-or-nothing signals and the firing-rate code

highlights.label: Learning
highlights.desc: Fire together, wire together, and how memories fade

title: The Memory Palace
outcomeTitle: Build a memory palace and test it for real
outcome: A memory palace for five things you want to learn, a real recall test, and a review plan.
description: Before paper, people held whole speeches in their heads using places they knew well. You'll pick five things worth remembering, build a route through a place you know, test your recall with the answers hidden, fix what didn't stick, and use the method on your own studying.
studyNote: Bring five things from a course you're studying; you'll use them in the last step.

highlights.label: Your palace
highlights.desc: Five items and a route through a place you know

highlights.label: Scenes that stick
highlights.desc: Associations you can rebuild from the place alone

highlights.label: A real test
highlights.desc: Recall with the answers hidden, then repair the gaps

highlights.label: Your studying
highlights.desc: Use it on real material, with a spaced review plan
